item.description: Celebrating 70 years of Eurovision at the National Science and Media Museum. Go behind the sequins of the world’s largest live music event and discover how the magic really happens.

item.description: Be part of a night like no other at the Bradford Alhambra as we bring you the concert you’ve been dreaming of! The ultimate celebration of one the biggest bands to have ever graced the stage – Queen.

item.description: Expect an exciting mix of lyrical melodies, rich harmonies, and dynamic improvisation and extraordinary axemanship as the John Bailey Quartet comes to JATP Jazz at the Bradford Latvian Club

item.title: The Coral
item.description: The Coral's mix of music hall, West Coast psychedelia, merseybeat, folk, jangle pop, garage rock, dub, reggae and more set them apart from their landfill contemporaries of the mid-noughties. The group continue to explore, experiment and evolve.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black History Month 2026 – Winter Garden Celebrations
item.description: Over three days expect to be entertained, informed and delighted by a powerful mix of music, storytelling, tasty food and fashion, plus free face painting for the children. Family friendly, accessible and all communities welcomed.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Wonder Stuff and Inspiral Carpets
item.description: Join the Wonder Stuff as they celebrate their 40th anniversary, supported by their old friends, Inspiral Carpets.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Americana: Gershwin & Bernstein for Trumpet
item.description: Award-winning rising star trumpeter Matilda Lloyd joins Music in the Round's resident Ensemble 360 for a sparkling celebration of American music, alongside some dazzling trumpet classics.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Jess & Rich Arrowsmith
item.description: Sheffield legends Jess and Rich Arrowsmith launch their new album As Merry As May Be.

item.title: Tchotchke
item.description: Drawing on the sass and attitude of 60s girl groups, the theatrics of outsider pop acts like Sparks and Harry Nilsson and the canonical pop hooks of the Beach Boys, this New York trio present their own candy-coated take on rock’n’roll.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Britallica
item.description: The world’s first Britney Spears metal tribute. Bringing Britney’s biggest pop anthems into the world of heavy metal – and where better for it than Corp, Sheffield's home of all things rock and alt.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Thomas Carter & Geb
item.description: A spellbinding evening of contemporary folk in the atmospheric Samuel Worth Chapel.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Rory Green
item.description: Beautiful atmospheric music full of layered sounds and infectious rhythms. Ghanaian-English guitarist, composer and producer Rory Green joins Jazz at The Lescar following appearances at Lancaster Jazz Festival and Manchester Jazz Festival.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Martin Simpson Trio
item.description: Legendary guitarist and songwriter Martin Simpson comes to Sheffield with his Some Kind of Jubilee tour.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: No Bounds
item.description: A weekend of bleeps, beats and sweaty grins – exploring the relationship between music, art, technology and place. The 2026 lineup includes: Mark Fell, Blawan, Oppidan, The Black Dog and lots more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.description: Following the triumph of their last concert, The Bootleg Beatles return to St. George's Hall with their focus on The Beatles top five selling albums.

item.ify:location: St Georges Hall, Bridge Street, Bradford, West Yorkshire, BD1 1JT

item.title: Eddi Reader
item.description: Celebrating over 40 years as a live performer, Eddi Reader has effortlessly developed into one of popular music’s most thrilling and affecting performers.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Jazzing for Jamaica
item.description: A celebration of Jamaican culture, music, and community spirit, raising funds for the Jamaican Hurricane Appeal. Headlining the evening will be the internationally acclaimed Michael "Bammi" Rose Quartet.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black-Owned Markets
item.description: Cutlery Works showcases black-owned businesses with over 12 stall holders offering a range of products, from beauty, fashion to baked goods. With live music and entertainment.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Orchestra Baobab
item.description: An institution of African music, led by Nick Gold of Buena Vista Social Club. More than 50 years on from their formation, the group’s mix of Afro-Cuban rhythms, Wolof griot traditions, mbalax, Congolese rumba and jazz, sounds as fresh as ever.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Jeff Wayne’s Musical Version Of The War Of The Worlds Live! Concert Experience
item.description: The martians invade Bradford Live
item.location: Bradford Live, 1 Thornton Road, Bradford, West Yorkshire, BD1 2EP
item.ify:location: Bradford Live, 1 Thornton Road, Bradford, West Yorkshire, BD1 2EP
item.dc:creator: Visit Bradford

item.title: Boyband In The Buff
item.description: Boyband in the Buff is the ultimate throwback concert with a cheeky twist - starring pop heartthrob Gareth Gates - and it's coming to St. George's Hall.
item.location: St Georges Hall, Bridge Street, Bradford, West Yorkshire, BD1 1JT
item.ify:location: St Georges Hall, Bridge Street, Bradford, West Yorkshire, BD1 1JT
item.dc:creator: Visit Bradford

item.title: Vaughan Williams: Songs of Travel
item.description: Music in the Round’s Singer-in-Residence Roderick Williams returns with a programme of heartrendingly beautiful English song, including Vaughan Williams’ glorious cycle Songs of Travel.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tangram: Rituals for a Changing World
item.description: From the intimate to the divine: an intriguing musical exploration of Chinese music and philosophy alongside European classical traditions in the Crucible Playhouse with Music in the Round.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Charlie Chaplin: The Gold Rush
item.description: Charlie Chaplin’s most ambitious and successful silent comedy presented in a gorgeous restoration. With Chaplin’s own Academy Award-nominated score, performed live by Music in the Round residents, Ensemble 360 and friends, conducted by George Morton.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Lady Leshurr – 10 Years of The Queen's Speech
item.description: The rapper and producer heads out on tour this autumn to celebrate the 10th anniversary of The Queen’s Speech series with a special run of intimate headline shows.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sensoria
item.description: Sheffield's festival of film and music. Expect a truly unique mix of performance, live film scores, screenings, exhibitions, and music industry activity. Come back soon for details of the Sensoria 2026 lineup.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beethoven & Brahms String Quartets
item.description: Opus 13, the most recent winner of the prestigious Wigmore Hall International String Quartet competition, makes its Sheffield debut with a programme of bold and lyrical works.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Soul II Soul
item.description: The iconic band born from the vibrant UK sound system culture. Emerging in the multicultural melting pot of London, Soul II Soul transformed ordinary house parties into extraordinary experiences with their innovative and immersive performances.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black History Month Community Civic Service
item.description: Sheffield Cathedral host the third annual Community Civic Service for Black History Month. With inspiring local speakers from the city’s Black-led churches, powerful gospel music, and information stands from community organisations.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Cabaret Voltaire
item.description: The iconic Sheffield band return to the Octagon, for the final date of their final tour.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: We Were Here: Stephanie Phillips
item.description: A reclamation of alternative music history, for the Black artists who helped pioneer and shape it. Stephanie Phillips is a music journalist and musician who started Black feminist punk band Big Joanie and is part of the Decolonise Fest collective.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Witching Tale, Jan Doyle Band & The Greystone Sisters
item.description: A mysterious, spellbinding Halloween show at the Samuel Worth Chapel, featuring The Witching Tale.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tim Burton’s Universe by Mystery Ensemble
item.description: What better way to celebrate Halloween than an evening of the weird, wonderful and slightly macabre sounds of Tim Burton’s longtime collaborator Danny Elfman. With music from The Nightmare Before Christmas, Edward Scissorhands, Beetlejuice and more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Mariam sings Amadou & Mariam
item.description: Hear Mariam’s vibrant, Malian, worldbeat music on the Octagon stage.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Festival of the Mind
item.description: A biennial festival of new ideas. Bringing together the city's creative community and its academic minds through exhibitions, talks, screenings, performances and more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Elgar Piano Quintet
item.description: Pianist Martin Roscoe joins forces with the Brodskys, a quartet who have been performing for over 50 years to prizes and plaudits around the world.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sounds of Now: Saxophone & Electronics
item.description: Praised for his “urgently visceral” playing (Tempo), London-based Canadian saxophonist David Zucchi is joined by Robert Laidlow for a programme of innovative works for saxophone and live electronics.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Rachel Newton
item.description: Join the award winning singer, harpist and composer in concert at Wild Traditions.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Chopin Nocturnes
item.description: "Poet of the piano” Pavel Kolesnikov is one of the world’s most exciting young pianists. Lauded for his amazing ability to cast new light on familiar repertoire, he makes his Music in the Round debut with a tour through Chopin's complete Nocturnes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: A Journey Through Nordic Music
item.description: Join a panel of musicians and experts who will shine a light on some of the composers and music featuring across Northern Lights, Music in the Round's weekend of elemental music from the frozen north.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Music from Iceland
item.description: A dazzling portrait of contemporary Icelandic music ranging from celebrated glacial works by Anna Thorvaldsdóttir and Oscar-winning Hildur Guðnadóttir, to new arrangements of Björk and Ólafur Arnalds’ haunting music for Broadchurch.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bob Dylan
item.description: Widely acknowledged as one of the most important figures of the modern day and one of the greatest and most influential songwriters of all time, Bob Dylan has reshaped popular music by elevating lyric writing to a profound literary art form.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Sibelius & Grieg
item.description: Music in the Round's resident Ensemble 360 performs masterpieces and miniatures for strings and piano by two giants of Nordic classicism.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Engegård Quartet
item.description: Norway’s multi-award-winning Engegård Quartet brings its customary boldness, energy and freshness to Sheffield in a concert of Mozart, Beethoven and Grieg.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Norwegian Folk
item.description: Formed under the midnight sun in the Lofoten Islands, Norway’s leading string quartet brings the rugged soul of the country to the stage, with arrangements of traditional joiks, haunting psalms and spirited bridal marches.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Snowman + Live Score
item.description: Unite the Union Brass Band present a special festive performance of the Christmas classic with a live score.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beethoven Appassionata
item.description: Tim Horton performs an afternoon concert for Music in the Round, launching his a journey through Beethoven’s staggering achievements for piano, with works including his celebrated Appassionata sonata.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Reich: Electric Counterpoint
item.description: Scottish guitarist Sean Shibe presents a tour of four centuries of music, including Bach’s first cello suite, Steve Reich’s masterpiece Electric Counterpoint and a recent commission by the UK’s leading contemporary composer Thomas Adès.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Arbrevyn
item.description: Arbrevyn perform a Christmas special concert. Featuring Cornish carols alongside more local carols and some of their favourite repertoire.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places
